name: Gearbox
text: Switch to the NVIDIA H100 with Llama 3.4 70B. It’s the fastest closed-source model we can run locally, cutting inference time by ~15% over the current setup. The trade-off is higher hardware cost and power draw, but the gain in throughput justifies it for EXCAVA’s scaling needs.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t just the higher hardware cost or lock-in—it’s that Llama 3.4 70B’s accuracy gains over our current model may not justify the 15% speed bump. A better alternative: test both models on EXCAVA’s critical tasks before committing; settle the argument with side-by-side benchmark results showing which delivers the net capability gain.

name: Gearbox
text:
Run a controlled A/B test: run Llama 3.4 70B on the NVIDIA H100 against the current model on EXCAVA’s top three critical tasks, using identical prompts and strict accuracy metrics. The trade-off is a one-time 4-hour delay to gather data, but it removes guesswork—we either confirm the 15% speed gain is worth the cost or we avoid a bad bet. If the new model wins, we switch; if not, we keep the current setup and save the hardware/power spend.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t just the 4-hour delay—it’s that the A/B test assumes identical prompts and metrics will expose the accuracy gap, but EXCAVA’s real-world performance depends on dynamic, unseen edge cases. A better alternative: run a shadow test where both models process live traffic in parallel for 24 hours, logging all discrepancies and downstream effects; settle the argument with hard data on actual user impact, not lab conditions.
